summary: printf and String.format build text from values, with control over decimal places, column width, and alignment. Use them for reports, receipts, and tables.
notes: %.2f shows 2 decimal places. It does not change the value stored in average.
%-12s pads the text to 12 characters, lined up on the left. %6.1f uses 6 characters, lined up on the right.
printf does not end the line. Put %n at the end of the format.
pitfall: Using %d for a double throws IllegalFormatConversionException: d != java.lang.Double. Use %f for double and %d for int.
